title: Rolling & Crawling Challenges
strapline: A tunnel to wriggle through, a cushion hill to climb, a treasure just out of reach — good reasons to get moving.
intent: Give pre-walkers rich, motivating reasons to roll, wriggle, commando-crawl and crawl — the movements that build the whole body.
Turn the floor into a gentle obstacle world: soft slopes, tunnels, low steps and textures that invite the next bit of moving.
Develop core strength, coordination and the cross-body crawling pattern that supports so much later learning.
Feed spatial exploration — over, under, through, behind — as babies discover where their bodies can go.
Build confidence and determination as a baby works out how to reach the thing they want.
implementation: Create a safe, soft movement area with cushions, wedges, a low tunnel, textured mats and sturdy things to pull up on.
Place treasures and mirrors just beyond easy reach, so there is always a reason to travel a little further.
Get down on the floor and crawl alongside — babies move more, and more happily, with a companion.
Vary the surfaces and levels — a squashy cushion, a firm mat, a gentle slope — for varied effort and balance.
Keep the space clear of hazards, cushion the hard edges, and stay close for the tumbles as babies test new moves.
key_questions: Can you reach the mirror if you wriggle a little further?
Where does the tunnel go — shall I meet you at the other end?
Can you climb up over the cushion hill?
Look how you rolled all the way over!
What's hiding behind here for you to find?

impact.text: Babies roll, wriggle and crawl to get where they want to go, gaining control of their bodies in sequence.
A baby climbs over cushions, crawls through the tunnel and pulls up on the sofa, exploring freely with the whole body.
Reaching, wriggling and travelling towards a treasure, babies explore space — over, under, through and behind.
With their key person close and crawling alongside, a baby ranges further and checks back with a look.

enhancements: A fabric play-tunnel with a treasure or a face waiting at the far end.
A cushion-and-wedge hill to climb over and roll down.
A low mirror at floor level that draws a baby to crawl towards their own reflection.
A treasure trail — objects set at intervals so each one invites a little more travel.
Different textured mats laid in a path — furry, bumpy, smooth — for varied crawling underhand.

playing_exploring: The baby explores where their body can go, choosing what to reach, roll to and crawl through.
Whole-body movement is the play — over, under, through, up and down.
active_learning: Babies work hard at a new move, trying again and again until the wriggle becomes a crawl.
creating_thinking: A baby works out a route to the treasure — round the cushion, through the tunnel — and follows it.
